text.p: Powerful thunderstorms lashed the upper Midwest on Wednesday, knocking out power for 50,000 people, swamping streets and delaying plane flights.
In St. Paul, an apartment building collapsed, dropping one resident two stories. She survived with minor injuries.

Forecasters said cooler, drier air colliding with hot, humid conditions produced storms across the region from Minnesota to Michigan. Severe thunderstorm warnings were issued for parts of Michigan's Upper Peninsula at mid-day on Wednesday, with some storms carrying wind gusts clocked at 60 mph (96.5 km).

The Minneapolis-St. Paul area was hit by heavy rains late Tuesday and into the night. At one point 3 inches (7.6 cm) of rain fell in 30 minutes. Electrical power was knocked out to more than 50,000 customers in the area and widespread flash flooding was reported.
Intersections were swamped stranding motorists in cars and strong winds uprooted trees. Flights were delayed for up to 90 minutes at the Minneapolis-St. Paul airport.
